intent: Communicate how far a task has progressed, or that work is still running when progress cannot be measured.
typical_uses: A long-running task with a known percentage
A task of unknown duration, marked indeterminate with `value={null}`

dont_use_when.situation: A short async action with no meaningful percentage

instead.note: On a Button, the `loading` prop carries the busy state inline (aria-busy) without a second element.

dont_use_when.situation: A placeholder for content that has not arrived, with nothing to measure
Step-by-step navigation where the steps are themselves the interface

instead.target: the consuming application's own step indicator
instead.note: The kit ships no stepper or wizard component, and a bar cannot carry per-step state or navigation.

invariants.text: Progress always renders its own track and indicator, after any children; there is no prop to suppress them. Children are the parts that belong beside the bar - a label, a readout - never a second track.

`value={null}` marks the bar indeterminate: the root reports no `aria-valuenow`, and every part of the family carries `data-indeterminate`, which the stylesheet turns into a sweeping band instead of a width fill.
The root element is what receives the accessible name: an `aria-label` on Progress, or a ProgressLabel child whose id the root wires into `aria-labelledby`.

anti_patterns.dont: Render one with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or compose a ProgressLabel into it; a bar reports a value but needs a name for what the progress is of

anti_patterns.dont: Fake an indeterminate look with a stuck value
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `value={null}` - a static value reports a false, frozen percentage to assistive technology

a11y.by: Base UI's own Progress primitive (role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/-min/-max wiring, and a ProgressLabel's id wired into aria-labelledby) plus progress.test.tsx's own accessible-name, aria-valuenow/-min/-max and data-indeterminate assertions

value.states: value is a number or null
value.because: `number | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a number-or-null union is left unasserted.

getAriaValueText.states: getAriaValueText is a function the root calls for the value's text alternative, not a value
getAriaValueText.because: `(formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null) => string` - a function of the formatted readout and the raw value. No JSON Schema type covers a function.

format.states: format is an Intl.NumberFormatOptions object controlling how the value is formatted
format.because: An object type with the full breadth of Intl's own formatting options is not something this schema restates; the kit forwards it to Base UI unchanged.

locale.states: locale is a BCP 47 locale string, an Intl.Locale object, or a readonly array of either, passed to Intl.NumberFormat
locale.because: Intl.LocalesArgument is a union of those shapes; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so this union is left to tsc.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Composed with a caption and a live readout

bad.title: A bar with no name
bad.why: The progressbar has no accessible name, so assistive technology announces a bare percentage with no name for what it is the progress of.
